meta.methodology: Severity (higher/moderate/lower registered-case rate) is calculated as registered cyber crime FIR cases per 1,00,000 population, using official NCRB case data and UIDAI projected population figures. researchPaper.researchTitle: State Threat Research: Customer Care Search Engine Spoofing & Utility Phishing in Bihar
researchPaper.stateRelevance: Bihar recorded 4,450 cybercrime FIRs in 2023, representing a 214.9% increase from 2021 (1,413 cases). Cyber fraud hubs frequently utilize SEO poisoning to list fake helpline numbers for banks, gas agencies, and courier services.
researchPaper.executiveSummary: Cyber criminals manipulate search engine search results and Google Maps business listings by inserting their fraudulent mobile numbers as 'Official Helpline' for major public banks, LPG gas providers, and eCommerce delivery services. When unsuspecting victims call for refund/support, scammers install remote access apps to drain bank accounts.

modusOperandi.initialContact: Victims search Google or Google Maps for 'Customer Care Helpline Number' of a bank, wallet, or courier.
modusOperandi.socialEngineering: Scammers answer professionally, pretending to be senior support executives, and offer an immediate refund of ₹500 - ₹2,000.
modusOperandi.technicalExploitation: Victims are instructed to install AnyDesk, TeamViewer QuickSupport, or RustDesk from the Play Store and share the 9-digit session passkey.
modusOperandi.financialDiversion: Once remote access is established, scammers view the victim's OTPs and netbanking credentials on-screen, executing unauthorized funds transfers.

researchPaper.targeting: General public, online shoppers, bank account holders, and utility consumers.
researchPaper.financialMechanism: IMPS/UPI transfers executed via compromised netbanking sessions to interstate mule accounts.
researchPaper.technicalAnalysis: SEO poisoning involves creating hundreds of transient blog posts and map listings containing targeted keywords ('Bank Helpline', 'Refund Customer Care'). Combined with remote access tools, it bypasses traditional 2FA security controls by capturing OTPs directly from the victim's screen.
warningSigns: Helpline numbers listed as mobile numbers (starting with 9, 8, 7, 6) rather than official 1800 toll-free numbers
Customer care asking you to install AnyDesk, RustDesk, or TeamViewer on your phone
Requests to pay a ₹5 or ₹10 'processing fee' through a link to process a refund
researchPaper.governmentResponse: Bihar Cyber Police and RBI have published advisories warning citizens to fetch contact details ONLY from official bank websites or physical debit cards.
researchPaper.victimResponse: If remote access was granted, immediately turn off Wi-Fi/Mobile Data, uninstall the app, call 1930 to freeze bank accounts, and file a report on cybercrime.gov.in.
researchPaper.legalContext: IT Act Section 66D, Section 66C, and BNS Section 318.
researchPaper.limitations: Reflects official 2023 NCRB statistics.

researchPaper.researchTitle: State Threat Research: Electricity Bill Disconnection APK & Phishing SMS Fraud in Delhi NCR
researchPaper.stateRelevance: Delhi NCR recorded 407 cybercrime FIRs in 2023 in NCRB statistics. Cyber gangs target residents across New Delhi, South Delhi, and NCR suburbs with urgent SMS alerts threatening power or SIM card disconnection.
researchPaper.executiveSummary: Scammers send urgent SMS messages: 'Dear Consumer, your electricity power will be disconnected tonight at 9:30 PM because your previous month bill was not updated. Immediately contact Electricity Officer on 9x-xxxxxx'. Calling the number leads to remote app installation or phishing link execution.

modusOperandi.initialContact: Bulk SMS sent during late afternoon or evening hours claiming imminent utility disconnection.
modusOperandi.socialEngineering: Creating artificial panic by claiming power will be cut off at night when utility offices are closed.
modusOperandi.technicalExploitation: Scammers direct victims to pay a nominal ₹10 'update fee' via a malicious phishing link or download a custom `.apk` file.
modusOperandi.financialDiversion: The phishing link captures netbanking credentials, debit card CVV, and OTPs, initiating unauthorized transactions up to account limits.

researchPaper.targeting: Residential homeowners, elderly citizens, small business owners, and tenant families.
researchPaper.financialMechanism: Direct debit card CVV/OTP harvesting and IMPS funds transfer to mule accounts.
researchPaper.technicalAnalysis: Phishing pages impersonate power distribution companies (DISCOMs) using identical CSS graphics. Text fields collect credit/debit card numbers, PINs, and real-time OTPs via Webhook scripts.
warningSigns: SMS warnings of power disconnection sent from personal 10-digit mobile numbers rather than official TRAI-registered sender IDs (e.g. `DL-BSES` or `BYPL`)
Demands to pay bill updates or small fees through unofficial personal UPI IDs or APK links
Threats of immediate same-day disconnection at night
researchPaper.governmentResponse: Delhi Cyber Police, TRAI, and power distribution utilities (BSES, TPDDL) have issued joint public notices emphasizing that power companies NEVER send disconnection notices via personal mobile numbers.
researchPaper.victimResponse: Do NOT click the SMS link. Verify bill status directly on the official utility website or app. Report scam SMS on TRAI Sanchar Saathi portal and 1930.
researchPaper.legalContext: IT Act Section 66D, Section 66C, and BNS Section 318.
researchPaper.limitations: Reflects official NCRB registered FIR records.

researchPaper.researchTitle: State Threat Research: FII/FPI Institutional Stock Trading & Fake IPO Allocation Fraud in Karnataka
researchPaper.stateRelevance: Documented in state cyber police bulletins and NCRB statistics showing Karnataka registered 21,889 cybercrime FIRs in 2023. Cybercrime syndicates heavily target tech professionals and retail investors in urban hubs such as Bengaluru, Mysuru, and Mangaluru.
researchPaper.executiveSummary: Syndicates operating from interstate and international call hubs create fake WhatsApp and Telegram groups impersonating accredited Foreign Institutional Investors (FIIs) and Foreign Portfolio Investors (FPIs). Victims are enticed with claims of institutional block trading discounts and guaranteed 100% IPO shares allocation via custom web applications.

modusOperandi.initialContact: Unsolicited WhatsApp/Telegram invites or social media ads featuring photos of prominent SEBI-registered fund managers.
modusOperandi.socialEngineering: Daily posting of fabricated profit screenshots, artificial praise by bot accounts, and fake SEBI registration certificates.
modusOperandi.technicalExploitation: Victims are instructed to download web-based trading apps (hosted on unencrypted, recently registered domains) that simulate live market tickers and fake portfolio growth.
modusOperandi.financialDiversion: Funds are transferred via RTGS/NEFT to multiple layer-1 mule bank accounts registered under shell entities rather than SEBI-cleared clearing corporations.

researchPaper.targeting: IT professionals, corporate executives, senior citizens, and active retail stock traders.
researchPaper.financialMechanism: Multi-layered RTGS/NEFT bank transfers into shell company mule accounts followed by immediate conversion into cryptocurrency or withdrawal via overseas ATM networks.
researchPaper.technicalAnalysis: Custom web applications utilize obfuscated JavaScript, fake WebSockets for simulated market charts, and lack SEBI-mandated two-factor authentication (2FA). Domain WHOIS inspection reveals recent registrations (< 30 days) hosted on bulletproof offshore servers.
warningSigns: Guaranteed fixed returns or claims of 100% IPO allotment through informal messaging apps
Demands to transfer investment funds into personal or private private-limited bank accounts instead of SEBI recognized stock brokers
Inability to withdraw funds without paying bogus 'tax clearance' or 'profit-sharing' fees upfront
researchPaper.governmentResponse: Karnataka Cyber Police & I4C (MHA) have initiated coordination with SEBI to block over 1,200 fraudulent domain names and frozen mule bank accounts through the National Cyber Crime Reporting Portal (1930).
researchPaper.victimResponse: Immediately report the fraud to the 1930 National Cyber Crime Helpline within the Golden Hour to trigger bank account freezes. File an official complaint on cybercrime.gov.in and notify your primary bank's fraud monitoring cell.
researchPaper.legalContext: Prosecuted under IT Act Section 66D (Cheating by personation using computer resource), Section 66C (Identity theft), and Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) Section 318 (Cheating).
researchPaper.limitations: FIR data reflects registered cases in official records; unreported incidents and ongoing investigations are excluded from public totals.

researchPaper.researchTitle: State Threat Research: AI Deepfake Audio/Video Emergency Impersonation Fraud in Kerala
researchPaper.stateRelevance: Kerala recorded 3,295 cybercrime FIRs in 2023, representing a 426.4% surge from 2021 (626 cases). High NRI population density has led to targeted AI deepfake voice cloning frauds impersonating relatives living abroad.
researchPaper.executiveSummary: Cyber criminals utilize generative AI voice cloning software to replicate the exact voice of a victim's friend or relative residing in the Gulf or overseas. The scammer calls the victim via WhatsApp audio/video call, claiming an urgent medical emergency or legal detention demanding immediate funds transfer.

modusOperandi.initialContact: WhatsApp audio or video call from an international number displaying a profile picture of the victim's relative.
modusOperandi.socialEngineering: AI-generated voice clone speaks in the exact dialect and tone, claiming: 'I am at the airport police station/hospital, please send ₹1.5 Lakh immediately'.
modusOperandi.technicalExploitation: Voice audio samples harvested from public social media videos (Instagram Reels, YouTube) are trained on real-time text-to-speech AI models.
modusOperandi.financialDiversion: Urgent UPI or IMPS transfer requested into a third-party account under the pretext of a local friend's or lawyer's account.

researchPaper.targeting: Families of NRIs, senior citizens, and relatives of individuals working overseas.
researchPaper.financialMechanism: Real-time IMPS/UPI transfer to local mule accounts followed by immediate ATM cash withdrawal.
researchPaper.technicalAnalysis: Generative AI deepfake pipelines utilize zero-shot voice cloning algorithms capable of generating realistic Malayalam speech from 5-second audio samples. Video deepfakes use face-swapping models with added video compression artifacts to mask glitches.
warningSigns: Urgent distress calls from overseas relatives asking for money to be sent to an unfamiliar third-party account
Video calls with blurred background, lagging lip-sync, or unnatural eye blinking
Refusal to talk on a regular cellular voice line or answer secondary security questions
researchPaper.governmentResponse: Kerala Police Cyber Operations Wing and CERT-In have issued dedicated deepfake awareness guidelines urging citizens to establish a private 'family passcode' to verify emergency calls.
researchPaper.victimResponse: Hang up and call your relative directly on their original cellular phone number or contact another family member to verify. Report to 1930 Helpline.
researchPaper.legalContext: IT Act Section 66D, Section 66C, Section 66E, and BNS Section 319.

researchPaper.researchTitle: State Threat Research: Digital Arrest & Law Enforcement Impersonation Extortion in Telangana
researchPaper.stateRelevance: Telangana Cyber Security Bureau (TCSB) and NCRB 2023 statistics highlight Telangana as recording 18,236 cybercrime FIRs (47.88 per lakh population). High digital connectivity in Hyderabad and surrounding districts has led to targeted Digital Arrest extortion schemes.
researchPaper.executiveSummary: Perpetrators call victims claiming to be officials from the Telecom Regulatory Authority of India (TRAI), CBI, Narcotics Control Bureau (NCB), or Mumbai Police. They accuse the victim of sending illegal narcotics or human trafficking contraband in courier parcels and force them into video calls under 'Digital Arrest'.

modusOperandi.initialContact: Automated IVR call stating 'Your SIM card / mobile number will be disconnected within 2 hours due to illegal activities'.
modusOperandi.socialEngineering: Transfer to a scammer dressed in official police uniform sitting in a room styled like a police station, creating extreme panic and fear of immediate arrest.
modusOperandi.technicalExploitation: Skype/WhatsApp video calls used to isolate the victim continuously for 24-72 hours, preventing them from communicating with family or legal counsel.
modusOperandi.financialDiversion: Victims are coerced into transferring their lifetime savings into 'RBI Verification Accounts' or 'Supervision Escrow Accounts' under threat of immediate physical arrest.

researchPaper.targeting: Senior citizens, retired government officers, working professionals, and homemakers.
researchPaper.financialMechanism: Real-time RTGS/IMPS transfers into multiple layers of rented mule accounts across multiple states.
researchPaper.technicalAnalysis: Scammers utilize VoIP caller ID spoofing to make incoming calls appear as official police control room numbers. Virtual backgrounds and AI face filters are occasionally used to simulate official badges.
warningSigns: Claims of 'Digital Arrest' via Skype or WhatsApp video call (Indian law enforcement NEVER conducts judicial arrest via video call)
Demands to keep the phone call connected continuously without telling family members or police
Directives to deposit money into bank accounts for 'judicial clearance' or 'CBI asset verification'
researchPaper.governmentResponse: Telangana Cyber Security Bureau (TCSB) in coordination with MHA I4C has issued state-wide public alerts and blocked over 3,000 SIM cards and IMEI numbers associated with Digital Arrest syndicates.
researchPaper.victimResponse: Disconnect the call immediately. Do NOT transfer any money. Immediately call 1930 or report to your local Cyber Crime Police Station.
researchPaper.legalContext: IT Act Section 66D, Section 66C, BNS Section 308 (Extortion), and BNS Section 319 (Impersonation).
researchPaper.limitations: Reflects official NCRB registered FIRs; real-time incident reports are updated continuously via 1930.

researchPaper.researchTitle: State Threat Research: Illegal Micro-Loan APK Blackmail & Remote Access Fraud in Uttar Pradesh
researchPaper.stateRelevance: Uttar Pradesh registered 10,794 official cybercrime FIRs in 2023 (NCRB report). Given the large digital user base across Noida, Lucknow, Kanpur, and Varanasi, predatory mobile loan applications and APK phishing are heavily reported.
researchPaper.executiveSummary: Victims are lured via short-video advertisements offering instant, zero-documentation loans up to ₹50,000. Upon downloading the Android application (outside the official Google Play Store via direct APK links), the malware silently exfiltrates contact lists, SMS logs, and gallery photos to extortion servers.

modusOperandi.initialContact: Social media ads, SMS links, or messaging pop-ups advertising 'Instant 5-Minute Emergency Loans'.
modusOperandi.socialEngineering: Only a small fraction (e.g. ₹3,000 out of ₹7,000) is disbursed, and within 4 days extortionists demand 300% repayment.
modusOperandi.technicalExploitation: The APK requests invasive Android permissions (`READ_CONTACTS`, `READ_SMS`, `READ_EXTERNAL_STORAGE`, `CAMERA`) during installation.
modusOperandi.financialDiversion: Failure to pay leads to automated morphing of victim gallery photos into offensive images, which are then broadcast to the victim's entire contact list.

researchPaper.targeting: Students, small shopkeepers, gig workers, and individuals needing urgent credit.
researchPaper.financialMechanism: UPI transfers to payment gateway merchant accounts linked to untraceable shell entities.
researchPaper.technicalAnalysis: Static and dynamic APK analysis reveals hardcoded C2 (Command & Control) server IPs, background contact list exfiltration via HTTP POST requests, and embedded RAT (Remote Access Trojan) capabilities.
warningSigns: Loan applications downloaded via direct `.apk` links instead of official app stores
Apps requesting permissions to access your personal phonebook contacts, SMS, and photo gallery
Unsolicited loan credit followed by immediate harassment and extortion within 3-5 days
researchPaper.governmentResponse: UP Cyber Crime Police and RBI have taken down hundreds of illegal loan apps and issued advisory alerts instructing citizens never to grant contact/photo permissions to financial apps.
researchPaper.victimResponse: Do NOT pay extortion demands. Revoke app permissions, uninstall the malicious APK, inform your family/contacts, and register a complaint on 1930 / cybercrime.gov.in.
researchPaper.legalContext: IT Act Section 66E (Violation of privacy), Section 67 (Publishing obscene material), Section 66D, and BNS Section 308 (Extortion).
researchPaper.limitations: Case figures based on 2023 NCRB official FIR records.
